{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2026}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 1987 | image = | dates = 24 May – 6 September 1987 | teams = 15 | connacht = | munster = Tipperary | leinster = Kilkenny | ulster = | matches = 17 | poty = [[File: Colours of Galway.svg|border|20px]] [[Joe Cooney]] | team = Galway | titles = 3rd | captain = [[Conor Hayes]] | manager = [[Cyril Farrell]] | team2 = Kilkenny | captain2 = [[Paddy Prendergast (hurler)|Paddy Prendergast]] | manager2 = [[Pat Henderson (hurler)|Pat Henderson]] | totalgoals = 61 (3.58 per game) | totalpoints = 500 (29.41 per game) | topscorer = [[File: Colours of Tipperary.svg|border|20px]] [[Pat Fox]] (3–45) | previous = [[1986 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1986]] | next = [[1988 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1988]] }} The '''1987 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 101st staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter county|inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. The championship began on 24 May 1987 and ended on 6 September 1987. [[Cork GAA|Cork]] were the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1986|defending champions]] but were defeated by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the Munster [[1987 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|final]]. [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] fielded a team in the provincial championship for the first time since 1978. On 6 September 1987, [[Galway GAA|Galway]] won the championship following a 1–12 to 0–9 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the 100th All-Ireland final. This was their third All-Ireland title, their first in seven championship seasons. Tipperary's [[Pat Fox]] was the championship's top scorer with 3–45. Galway's [[Joe Cooney]] was the choice for [[Texaco Hurler of the Year]]. == Team changes == === To Championship === Qualified from the [[All-Ireland Senior B Hurling Championship]] * [[London county Murray]] (Limerick) }} {{main|1987 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final}} ---- ==Championship statistics== ===Miscellaneous=== * [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] take part in the Munster series of games for the first time since 1978. * In the Munster semi-final replay against [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]], [[Cork GAA|Cork]]'s [[John Fenton (hurler)|John Fenton]] scored, what is often regarded as, one of the greatest hurling goals of all-time. Playing in his usual midfield position he struck the sliotar on the ground and scored a goal from forty-five yards out. In 2005 this goal was listed as one of [[RTÉ]]'s [[Top 20 GAA Moments]] and, in a [[TG4]] poll in 2009 it was voted the second greatest hurling goal of all-time. * At the [[1987 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster final]] between [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] the official attendance is given as 56,005. Two gates, however, were broken down before the start of the game and an estimated 3,000 people gained free entry to the Killinan terrace. * The Leinster final between [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] and [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] is postponed due to damage to the [[Croke Park]] pitch following a [[U2]] [[The Joshua Tree Tour|concert]] in June. ===Top scorers=== ;Overall {| class="wikitable" |- !
